_about: The words of the site, one file per language (the list and its order — src/langs.json). site — the main page (src/index.html, 404, the music card); brand — the brand page /brand/ (src/brand.html, keys b.…); cubepix — only in a language the CubePix site does not speak yet (see below). English (this file) is the reference: every other language translates every key, and npm test (the build with --strict) fails on a missing, empty or extra one. Never translated: Lewydo, «Love What You Do», game names, Google Play, file names, code in `backticks`, numbers, colours. **bold**, *emphasis*, `code` and [text](url) stay as they are; {n} is the number of a plural string {one, few, many, other…} — the forms of the language (Intl.PluralRules), each with {n}. lang.stop is the games’ own words (Orbit Dash i18n, «Russia, stop the war in Ukraine»). Words about CubePix (cp:…) come from the CubePix site itself (src/cubepix.json, npm run cubepix). A language that site does not have yet gets them here, in «cubepix»: { S: the keys of src/cubepix.json → S.en, pics: { painting: { n, a, y (, f) } } } — the build takes the snapshot first, then this supplement, and fails if neither has a word (the snapshot never touches these files). Edit here, then npm run build.

site.p.vlad.bio: Writing code since 2017: Java first, Kotlin a year later. A full-time game developer since 2021, from trainee all the way to Team Lead at a game studio. Every Lewydo game is built with Kotlin and LibGDX, Android first.
site.p.lilya.bio: Websites, presentation design and social media visuals are her main field. Thanks to Vlad she stepped into game design too, and every Lewydo game carries her touch. *Between us: websites are still her first love* 😉
site.story.title: Our story so far
site.story.1.d: Vlad writes his first code. A year later he switches to Kotlin and stays with it for good.
site.story.2.d: Vlad leaves the Military Institute of Telecommunications behind and goes full-time into games: trainee, junior… all the way to Team Lead.
site.story.3.d: A developer meets a designer. The studio doesn't know it exists yet.
site.story.4.d: Same day, different month — a team forever.
site.story.brand.d: Vlad always ended his [Medium](https://veldan1202.medium.com/) articles on LibGDX, Android and Kotlin the same way: «Love what you do» and a green heart 💚. That sign-off became our brand.
site.story.imc.d: IMC: Idle Merge Cubes 2026 is released on Google Play.
site.story.idea.d: Vlad is serving in the Armed Forces of Ukraine. One morning he wakes up in a house where his unit is staying on an assignment — with the idea of CubePix in his head.
site.story.od.d: We make Orbit Dash and publish it on Google Play: two orbits, one tap.
site.story.proto.d: The first playable prototype: famous paintings revealed cube by cube.
site.story.pix.d: We invent the CubePix mascot: a little pink painter cube with a beret and a brush. His name is Pix — Cube + Pix = CubePix, so the game carries his name.
site.story.l10n.d: Our biggest job yet: the studio site, both game sites and the games themselves — CubePix and Orbit Dash — learn 82 languages, so everyone can play in their own. For twelve days the laptop never switched off. Two Claude accounts worked side by side: one was paid by the game company where Vlad was a Team Lead ($120), the other was on Lilya's email ($120) — and when every weekly limit ran out, it grew into a $200 Max ×20 plan. One account built prototypes on the web straight from GitHub; the other ported what was finished into the real Android and iOS games. At that company, Vlad's colleagues — developers Nasuf and Taras — were great guys; it's a pity that once Claude Code got this good, layoffs followed.
site.story.l10n.d2: That's when our rule was born: Prototype → Game, never the other way round. Nothing changes in a game directly — first the prototype, then the game, so whatever we see in the prototype is exactly what's in the game. We hope you'll feel the difference in your own language.
site.story.l10n.photo: The desk in those days: the laptop that ran for twelve days straight, with the Android and iPhone test phones beside it.
site.story.live.d: Andrii (TikTok @malcev_ua) plays Orbit Dash in a TikTok LIVE — the first streamer ever to go live with our game.
site.story.live.video: Andrii plays Orbit Dash live on TikTok
site.story.live.thanks: Thank you, Andrii, for being my first streamer to go live playing my game. Thank you so much!
site.story.web.t: The web becomes a real platform
site.story.web.d: After that stream, Vlad starts taking the web seriously. Until then we made games only for phones — Android and iOS — and the web version of Orbit Dash was just a demo to get a taste of the game. But streamers and players clearly want to play on a computer too, so Vlad takes on a full port to the browser.
site.story.web.d2: Now we have one more platform: Orbit Dash and CubePix are the full games on the web as well — nothing to install, just open and play.
site.story.web.photo: Orbit Dash and CubePix in the browser — the same full games as on phones.
site.story.sale.d: Someone from Italy buys REMOVE ADS in Orbit Dash for $3.99 — and $3.03 reaches us. The first dollars our games have ever earned. Grazie mille! 🇮🇹
site.story.ios.t: Orbit Dash goes to the App Store
site.story.ios.d: For the first time, a Lewydo game is sent to App Store review — Orbit Dash for iPhone and iPad, with all 82 languages and RANKS. Fingers crossed! 🤞
site.story.next.d: CubePix is out on Google Play, and Pix arrives straight in his Halloween costume: the whole museum celebrates until November 30.

brand.meta.title: Lewydo™ brand — the heart, the splash, the menu signature, About us
brand.meta.desc: How to recognise Lewydo, and everything a Lewydo game needs to show it the same way: the mark, colours, the splash screen, the menu signature, About us and the heartbeat — with the assets and the code.
brand.nav.label: Brand page
brand.hero.title: One heart, the same everywhere
brand.hero.sub: How to recognise Lewydo — and everything a Lewydo game needs to show it the same way: the mark, its colours, the splash screen, the menu signature, About us and the heartbeat. The pictures and the code are right here, free to use in Lewydo projects.
brand.hero.replay: Play the splash with its sound
brand.rec.title: How to recognise Lewydo
brand.rec.sub: A hand-drawn green heart shaped like a speech bubble, glowing mint on deep night blue, with a round white name under it. Wherever you see it, the game was made by the two of us, with love.
brand.part.heart.d: Drawn by hand, shaped like a speech bubble: dark ink, a green fill with a chalky texture, a few splashes of paint.
brand.part.glow.d: A soft mint glow (#6DF593) around the heart — it is part of the mark, never a separate effect.
brand.part.name.d: «Lewydo» in Nunito Black, white, with a soft shadow.
brand.part.slogan.d: «Love What You Do» — always in English, it is a trademark. Its bold letters spell the name.
brand.part.line.d: A thin white line, 146 wide, that closes the mark.
brand.spell: The name is made of the slogan: the bold letters of «Love What You Do» read **Lewydo**. That is why the slogan is never translated.
brand.where.1.d: The splash screen: the Lockup appears, the heart beats once.
brand.where.2.t: At the bottom of every menu
brand.where.2.d: The signature pill — tap it to meet the studio.
brand.where.3.d: The Lockup above a few words about the two of us.
brand.where.4.d: [roshevasternin.github.io](/) — the heart built from the pixels of our games.
brand.rules.title: Keep it the same
brand.do.1: Use the pictures and the code of the kit **as they are**.
brand.do.2: Keep the colours, the font and the proportions: the Lockup is **208×322**, the signature **24 + name**.
brand.do.3: Let the heart **beat once** when the brand appears: the splash, About us (every time it opens), the menu pill.
brand.do.4: Theme the **background and the ambient light** to your game — the mark stays the same on top of it.
brand.do.5: Keep it on a dark background (#0E1024 or your game's own dark night).
brand.dont.1: Redraw, recolour, stretch, squash, rotate or add effects to the mark.
brand.dont.2: Translate the slogan or set the name in another font.
brand.dont.3: Loop the heartbeat — a logo that blinks forever distracts from the game.
brand.dont.4: Put it on a light or busy background.
brand.col.title: Night blue, a mint glow, a green heart
brand.col.sub: Tap a colour to copy it.
brand.sw.name: Name
brand.type.name: **Name** — Nunito Black 54, line 74, white, shadow 0 4 2 rgba(0,0,0,.25)
brand.type.slogan: **Slogan** — Nunito 14, line 19: L, e, W, Y, Do — Black, the rest — Regular
brand.type.pics: In apps the name and the slogan are **pictures** (the kit) — no font needed.
brand.text.1: About us text — Nunito Medium 15 / 23, width 312, centred
brand.text.thanks: The thank-you («Thank you for playing!») — its own last line under the text: centred, one line in every language (a long one gets smaller, it never wraps); Nunito ExtraBold 15 / 23, white
brand.text.2: Buttons — 296×52, radius 16; green #3DDC84 with #04120A text, or outlined
brand.games.title: The splash, the loader credits, About us, the menu signature
brand.games.sub: The same four places in every Lewydo game, 360×800. The mark and its numbers never change; the background and the light may follow the game — try it:
brand.ph.loader.d: Right after the splash, at the bottom of the game's loader (never on the splash itself): who made the game, on what, and which version. The version is the app's own, so it changes by itself with every release.
brand.ph.splash.d: The first screen of every game, ≈ 4 s: the mark arrives, then the heartbeat with the Lewydo sound, then the game's loader.
brand.ph.about.d: The heart beats every time About us opens. The text, the buttons and the back button are each game's own; the mark is the same.
brand.mn.title: YOUR GAME
brand.ph.menu.d: A quiet signature, not an ad: centred, 34 px from the bottom. Tap → About us (the pill presses to 0.96). It beats once when the menu appears — tap it here.
brand.num.1: **Lockup 208×322**: logo 208×208 (the glow fills it, the heart 140×140 in the middle) · name 208×74 · slogan 208×19 · line 146×1, 20 below
brand.num.2: **Splash**: the heart arrives 0.15→0.85 s · the name 0.55→1.1 and the slogan 0.85→1.4 come into focus · the line opens 1.15→1.85 · the finale: a breath in at 2.0, lub at 2.17, dub at 2.45, two waves of light · the sound from 2.09 · 3.8 s → the game
brand.num.3: **About us**: Lockup at top 108 · text at 456, width 312 · buttons 296×52 at 584 and 682 · the site address at 648 · © at 764
brand.num.4: **Signature pill**: 28 high, radius 999, border 1 px #3DDC84 24 %, fill 4 %, › 5×8 #9DF5C2 65 %, paddings 3 / 10, gap 5; tap area 48
brand.num.5: **Loader credits**: Powered by LibGDX · Developed by Lewydo™ · Version + the app's version — Inter Medium 10, line height 12, white 25 %, centred; a 360×36 block 28 above the bottom (+ safe area); English in every language
brand.hb.title: One beat, when the brand appears
brand.hb.sub: The heart and its glow beat **separately** — a quick «lub-dub» — exactly **once**: when the splash shows, every time About us opens, when the menu pill appears. Never in a loop. With «reduce motion» on, it doesn't beat at all.
brand.dl.title: The brand kit
brand.dl.sub: The pictures are the ones from Figma that the games use: PNG @3x of the sizes above, sharp on any screen. Apps take the PNGs or the whole LibGDX atlas; websites can take the WebP copies of the same pictures.
brand.dl.zip.d: Pictures (PNG + WebP), the sound, the LibGDX atlas, the Kotlin and web code, brand.json
brand.c.heart.d: brand_front (the heart) over brand_back (the glow) — two pictures, so they can beat separately. Logo box 208, heart 140.
brand.c.name: The name
brand.c.line.d: 146×1, 20 below the slogan; on the splash it opens from the middle.
brand.c.lockup.d: One transparent picture — for stores, videos and slides. In a game, build it from the parts (the splash animates them).
brand.c.pill.d: The menu pill from Figma, one transparent picture. In a game, build it from the parts, so the heart can beat.
brand.c.atlas.d: All five pictures in one texture — assets/atlas/, EnumAtlas.BRAND.
brand.c.code.d: LibGDX (Kotlin) for the games, CSS for the web — the splash, the heartbeat, the pill.
brand.dev.title: Put Lewydo into a new game
brand.dev.sub: Everything below lives in [the site’s repository → brand/](https://github.com/RoShevasternin/roshevasternin.github.io/tree/main/brand) and in [brand.json](/brand/brand.json) (all the numbers, the texts in every language of our games and the file addresses — for code and for Claude).
brand.step.1.d: Copy `kit/atlas/brand.atlas` + `brand.png` into `assets/atlas/` and `kit/sound/lewydo-heartbeat.wav` into `assets/sound/`; the atlas regions: `brand_back`, `brand_front`, `lewydo`, `slogan`, `brand_line` (your `assetsBrand`, `EnumAtlas.BRAND`).
brand.step.2.d: Copy `LewydoHeartbeat.kt` (package `com.lewydo.brand`) and `BrandScreen.kt`, `ABrandGroup.kt`, `ABrandLogo.kt`; replace `yourgame` with your package. They use the Lewydo LibGDX base (AdvancedScreen, AConstraintLayout, AAutoLayout).
brand.step.3.d: Start the game on `BrandScreen`: ≈ 4 s — the mark arrives, the heartbeat and the Lewydo sound, then `LoaderScreen`. Connect `soundVolume()` to your game's sound settings: 1.0 at their usual level, quieter only if the player turns sounds down.
brand.step.4.d: The pill at the bottom of the menu (centred, 34 px from the bottom) → About us; one beat when the menu appears.
brand.step.5.d: The Lockup at top 108, the studio text (English is the reference; every language of our games is in brand.json), «Our website» → `https://roshevasternin.github.io/` with the address under it, «Our games on Google Play» → our developer page, «© 2026 Lewydo™». One beat every time it opens.
brand.step.6.d: Theme the background and the light behind the mark to your game — never the mark itself.
brand.prompt: For Claude in another project — copy this (Claude reads it in English)
brand.foot: © 2026 Lewydo™ · Love What You Do. The Lewydo mark is ours: use it only in Lewydo projects, and only as this kit shows it.
brand.hb.finale: In the splash the beat is the **finale**: the whole mark arrives first, then a breath in, a big lub and a dub, two waves of light — and the Lewydo sound.
brand.snd.title: The sound of Lewydo
brand.snd.sub: Only the heart: two soft, round heartbeats — the first stronger, the second quieter — right on the beats of the mark. No melody, nothing ringing: a calm, warm hello.
brand.snd.r1: Once per launch, with the splash — never in a loop.
brand.snd.r2: At full volume when the game's sounds are at their usual level (gain 1.0); the player's slider may only make it quieter; sounds off — silence.
brand.snd.r3: Never change it, cut it or play it under music.
brand.snd.r4: A web page may play it only after a tap; a splash that opens by itself stays silent.
brand.snd.r5: One file everywhere: `lewydo-heartbeat.wav` — every game, its web prototype and its site play this very file, byte for byte. Lossless (16-bit PCM, 48 kHz, stereo) and made for phone speakers (its own overtones, peaks at −1 dBFS) — so Lewydo sounds the same wherever you hear it.
brand.say.note: «Lewydo» is «Love What You Do» said quickly: three syllables, **Lev-why-do**.
brand.c.sound.d: The heartbeat — one lossless .wav for games, web prototypes and sites. No .ogg or .mp3 copies: every device would decode them a little differently.
brand.dont.5: Play the sound in a loop, louder than the game, or when the player has turned sounds off.
brand.work.title: Prototype first, then the game
brand.work.lead: This is how every Lewydo game is made.
brand.work.1: **New things start in the prototype.** A screen, a mechanic, a text or a number is made and tried in the game's web prototype first — it's quick to test in a browser.
brand.work.2: **The game is ported from it.** The game (LibGDX: Android, later iOS) takes everything from the prototype, numbers and words one to one: the prototype is the reference.
brand.work.3: **Never the other way round.** Something new made only in the game is unknown to the prototype, and the two drift apart. Even a fix: first in the prototype, then in the game.
